9. // which are verified (or trusted) in their own modules. The shared spec
10. // vocabulary (`spec_addr`, `align_value`, `addr_is_aligned`, `addr_inv`) lives

1. // Copyright(c) The Maintainers of Nanvix.
2. // Licensed under the MIT License.
3. 
4. // `Address` trait — Specifications
5. //
6. // To callers, an `Address` is a single pointer-sized location in an address
7. // space: one mathematical integer in `[0, usize::MAX]`. The three in-scope
8. // trait methods form the raw-value boundary of that resource — project the
9. // abstract address back to a raw `usize` (`into_raw_value`), validate/construct
10. // one from a raw `usize` (`from_raw_value`), and query its alignment
11. // (`is_aligned`). See `view_design.md`.
12. //
13. // The abstract address is exposed through the universal projection `spec_addr`
14. // rather than `vstd::View`: `Address` cannot carry a `View<V = int>` supertrait
15. // because the per-implementor `View` impls (`PhysicalAddress`, `PageAligned`,
16. // `PageTableAligned`, ...) are `cfg(verus_keep_ghost)`-gated, so the bound would
17. // be unsatisfiable in a normal `cargo build` and would break the generic
18. // `impl<T: Address>` blocks (e.g. `region.rs`). This mirrors the kernel's own
19. // `spec_addr` / `spec_page_size` projections (`hal::mem`), which exist for the
20. // same reason and which this module is intended to subsume.
21. 
22. verus! {
23. 
24. // Universal abstract-address projection of any `Address` implementor: the
25. // pointer-sized numeric address it denotes (`int`).
26. //
27. // `uninterp` because there is no `View<V = int>` supertrait to define it
28. // concretely over a bare `T: Address` (see the module note above). It is not a
29. // free assumption: the trait-method contracts below pin it operationally — a
30. // value built by `from_raw_value(raw)` projects back through `into_raw_value`
31. // to exactly `raw`, and `is_aligned` reports `spec_addr` modulo the alignment.
32. // This is the standard logical-identity pattern, identical to the kernel's
33. // `hal::mem::spec_addr`; no `external_body` axiom feeds it.
34. //
35. // The generic parameter is intentionally *unbounded* (`T`, not `T: Address`).
36. // Bounding it by `Address` would make this projection part of the `Address`
37. // trait's own definition cycle (the trait-method contracts below reference
38. // `spec_addr`, which would in turn reference the trait), which Verus rejects as
39. // a cyclic self-reference. Callers always instantiate `T = Self` inside an
40. // `Address` context, so the bound is recovered at every use site.
41. pub uninterp spec fn spec_addr<T>(addr: &T) -> int;
42. 
43. // The pointer-sized well-formedness bound shared by every `Address`
44. // implementor. Refinement implementors (aligned / frame-representable) add
45. // their own predicate on top in their own `inv()`; only the universal bound
46. // belongs here. Unbounded `T` for the same cycle-avoidance reason as
47. // `spec_addr` above; instantiated at `T = Self` in every `Address` context.
48. pub open spec fn addr_inv<T>(addr: &T) -> bool {
49.     0 <= spec_addr(addr) <= usize::MAX as int
50. }
51. 
52. // The integer alignment named by an `Alignment` — the positive power of two
53. // that is its discriminant (`Align4 = 4`, ..., `Align4194304 = 4194304`).
54. pub open spec fn align_value(a: Alignment) -> int {
55.     a as int
56. }
57. 
58. // The single alignment fact `is_aligned` reports and that callers branch on:
59. // the address is an exact multiple of the alignment.
60. pub open spec fn addr_is_aligned(addr: int, a: Alignment) -> bool {
61.     addr % align_value(a) == 0
62. }
63. 
64. } // verus!
65.

33. //==================================================================================================

35. #[verus_verify]
36. pub trait Address
37. where
38.     Self: core::fmt::Debug + Clone + Copy + PartialEq + Eq + PartialOrd + Ord,
39. {
40.     ///
41.     /// # Description
42.     ///
43.     /// Instantiates a new [`Address`] from a raw value.
44.     ///
45.     /// # Parameters
46.     ///
47.     /// - `raw_addr`: The raw value.
48.     ///
49.     /// # Returns
50.     ///
51.     /// - `Ok(Self)`: The new address.
52.     /// - `Err(Error::BadAddress)`: If the provided address is invalid.
53.     ///
54.     // On success, the constructed address projects back to exactly the supplied
55.     // raw value (the inverse of `into_raw_value`) and satisfies the universal
56.     // pointer-sized bound. On failure, the value was outside this type's domain
57.     // and `Err(Error::BadAddress)` is returned. (`VirtualAddress` never fails;
58.     // refinement implementors fail on their own domain predicate.)
59.     #[verus_spec(result =>
60.         ensures
61.             match result {
62.                 Ok(a) => spec_addr(&a) == raw_addr as int && addr_inv(&a),
63.                 Err(e) => e.code == crate::error::ErrorCode::BadAddress,
64.             },
65.     )]
66.     fn from_raw_value(raw_addr: usize) -> Result<Self, Error>;
67. 
68.     // Total projection to the raw numeric address; never fails. Pure newtype
69.     // identity (`result as int == spec_addr(&self)`) — the inverse of
70.     // `from_raw_value`. This is the fact downstream crates pin as a trust
71.     // boundary today (`kernel`'s `phys.spec.rs` `assume_specification`).
72.     #[verus_spec(result =>
73.         ensures
74.             result as int == spec_addr(&self),
75.     )]
76.     fn into_raw_value(self) -> usize;
77.     ///
78.     /// # Description
79.     ///
80.     ///  Aligns the target [`Address`] to the provided `alignment`. If the address is already
81.     /// aligned, it is returned as is.
82.     ///
83.     /// # Parameters
84.     ///
85.     /// - `alignment`: The alignment to align the target address to.
86.     ///
87.     /// # Returns
88.     ///
89.     /// Upon success, the aligned address is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
90.     ///
91.     fn align_up(&self, align: Alignment) -> Result<Self, Error>;
92. 
93.     ///
94.     /// # Description
95.     ///
96.     /// Aligns the target [`Address`] down to the provided `alignment`. If the address is
97.     /// already aligned, it is returned as is.
98.     ///
99.     /// # Parameters
100.     ///
101.     /// - `alignment`: The alignment to align the target address to.
102.     ///
103.     /// # Returns
104.     ///
105.     /// Upon success, the aligned address is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
106.     ///
107.     fn align_down(&self, align: Alignment) -> Result<Self, Error>;
108. 
109.     ///
110.     /// # Description
111.     ///
112.     /// Checks if the target [`Address`] is aligned to the provided `alignment`.
113.     ///
114.     /// # Parameters
115.     ///
116.     /// - `alignment`: The alignment to check.
117.     ///
118.     /// # Returns
119.     ///
120.     /// Upon success, `true` is returned if the address is aligned, otherwise `false`. Upon failure,
121.     /// an error is returned instead.
122.     ///
123.     // The boolean is exactly the alignment predicate over the abstract address
124.     // (`b == spec_addr(self) % align == 0`); this is the only payload callers
125.     // branch on. `Alignment` is a closed enum of valid powers of two, so there
126.     // is no genuine failure condition: concrete implementors never take the
127.     // `Err` arm, and the contract pins this as total (`result is Ok`) so that
128.     // alignment guards (`mprotect`/`munmap`/`heap`/`PageAligned`) can rely on
129.     // the query succeeding.
130.     #[verus_spec(result =>
131.         ensures
132.             result is Ok,
133.             result->Ok_0 == addr_is_aligned(spec_addr(self), align),
134.     )]
135.     fn is_aligned(&self, align: Alignment) -> Result<bool, Error>;
136. 
137.     ///
138.     /// # Description
139.     ///
140.     /// Returns the maximum address for [`Address`].
141.     ///
142.     /// # Returns
143.     ///
144.     /// The maximum [`Address`].
145.     ///
146.     fn max_addr() -> usize;
147. 
148.     fn as_ptr(&self) -> *const u8;
149. 
150.     fn as_mut_ptr(&self) -> *mut u8;
151. }
